subject: Next steps: PoC mode choice and trial plan for Aurora Health
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Khan <elena.khan@aurorahealth.com>, Mark Dalton <mark.dalton@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + PoC options (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) — Aurora Health discovery

Hi Elena / Mark,

Thanks again for taking the call today — really appreciated the context on your imaging ingestion and PHI handling requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before drafting an SOW: 

Summary of options we discussed (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest to get started (hours), lowest setup cost, but would require Aurora to accept a hosted SaaS model and TTL-based data retention.
- Dedicated Capacity: reserved GPU pools under a contract — predictable throughput, data isolation inside our tenancy, and SLA options.
- Private (VPC or on-prem): customer-managed VPC with private control plane (or on-prem appliance) — most control for PHI, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit export.

From our discovery, I heard these as key constraints for you: PHI in flight and at rest controls, SSO & SCIM, ability to run audit logs into your SIEM, and a 3–4 week window for a technical PoC ahead of procurement. Please correct anything I got wrong.

Proposed PoC approach (short):
- Goal: Validate inference latency and data handling for 10k imaging-derived prompts/day and EHR-backed retrieval.
- Duration: 4–6 weeks (technical PoC)
- Success criteria (initial ask):
  - Latency: 95th percentile < 350ms for 128-token responses under batch sizes typical of production
  - Isolation: KV cache/inputs not retained beyond session; S3 encryption verified; KMS integration validated
  - Ops: Model rollout and rollback tested, and per-request tracing into your observability pipeline

Stakeholders to include on our side: Rafael (sales), Ben (solutions), Marissa (customer success). On your side, we recommend Eng/Platform, Security (for KMS/audit review), and a procurement lead.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm preferred deployment direction (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). If Private, confirm whether VPC-hosted is acceptable or if fully on-prem is required.
2) If Private/Dedicated, we’ll route a solutions brief + draft SOW (internal sec checklist attached) and schedule a 60–90 minute feasibility call with our infra lead.
3) We’ll share a tailored PoC playbook with concrete timelines and environment requirements.

I attached a short scoping deck (aurora_poc_scoping.pdf) and an internal checklist for our team to use. Happy to jump on a quick call to run through the options in more detail.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: aurora_poc_scoping.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)
From: Elena Khan <elena.khan@aurorahealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mark Dalton <mark.dalton@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + PoC options (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) — Aurora Health discovery

Thanks Rafael — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Compliance: Because we will be processing PHI, our security team has a strong preference for Private deployment (VPC first; on-prem only if VPC cannot meet our controls).
- Audit / KMS: We need to ensure that keys are under our control (bring-your-own-key) and that audit logs can be streamed to our Splunk instance. Do you support HSM-backed keys and Splunk forwarding?
- Timeline: Procurement would like a 6–8 week technical PoC to validate the above before moving to procurement/contracting. The PoC needs to include a short control validation checklist for our security reviewers.

If possible, please send a draft SOW and an estimate for Private VPC PoC work (including options for an on-prem fallback). Also propose up to three dates for the feasibility call with your infra/systems engineer.

Thanks — copying Mark (CTO) for visibility.

— Elena
Elena Khan
Director, AI Platforms
Aurora Health

Ben / Marissa,

Forwarding Elena's reply — Aurora is leaning toward Private VPC with BYOK/HSM and Splunk audit forwarding. Procurement wants a 6–8 week PoC. Action items I suggest: 

1) Ben: can you confirm our Private VPC playbook for HSM integration and whether we can expose KMS endpoints to a customer-managed key? Any design constraints we should flag?
2) Marissa: please draft a short SOW template for a 6-week Private PoC (deliverables, security validation checklist, success criteria, acceptance). I'll include Aurora-specific items (latency targets, KV cache retention rules).
3) I'll propose three feasibility-call times next week and loop in our infra lead (cc to be added once available).

I've attached our internal_poc_checklist.xlsx to make sure we hit all security items on the call.

Thanks — Rafael

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Khan <elena.khan@aurorahealth.com>, Mark Dalton <mark.dalton@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Private VPC PoC proposal & next steps — Aurora Health

Hi Elena / Mark,

Following up with a concrete PoC plan based on your preferences for Private VPC + BYOK: 

PoC summary (6-week technical PoC)
- Objective: Validate inference performance and security controls in a customer-managed VPC using BYOK (HSM option) and Splunk audit export.
- Timeline (proposed):
  Week 0: SOW sign & kick; exchange network details and KMS onboarding prep
  Week 1: Provision test VPC environment and demo baseline model in sandbox
  Weeks 2–4: Ingest sample imaging prompts, run throughput/latency tests, and run security control checks (KMS/HSM, audit forwarding)
  Week 5: Failure-mode testing, model rollout/rollback exercise, and cost baseline analysis
  Week 6: Acceptance testing and security sign-off; handoff to procurement/ops for next steps

Deliverables
- Configured Private VPC test environment (access details, runbook)
- PoC runbook with test harness and sample prompts
- Security validation report (KMS/HSM verification, Splunk ingestion confirmation, audit log snapshot)
- Performance report (latency percentiles, throughput, cost estimate)
- Draft SOW for the next phase (attached: sow_draft.docx)

Success criteria (finalized with your security team):
- 95th percentile latency < 350ms at target throughput
- BYOK/HSM key usage verified and key access controlled by Aurora
- Audit log forwarding to Splunk with sample events within 24 hours of ingestion
- Test KV cache retention verified per agreed TTL
- Signed acceptance form at PoC completion

Attachments included: sow_draft.docx, aurora_poc_scoping.pdf. For procurement ease I've also added links to the HubSpot deal and a preliminary DocuSign template: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/AU-2026-045 and https://www.docusign.com/examples/sow-au-2026

Next steps I need from you:
1) Confirm acceptance of the 6-week PoC timeline and success criteria (reply to this thread).
2) If accepted, Elena — please provide a primary technical contact and security reviewer and confirm three available windows for a 60–90m feasibility call next week.
3) Once confirmed, we'll route the SOW for signature (DocuSign link above) and schedule the infra call.

Happy to jump on a call to walk through the runbook.

Best regards,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sow_draft.docx (Word, 6 pages); aurora_poc_scoping.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)
